steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Conceptual lightning-tour of a Transformer

1. Tokens → Vectors  
   • Text (or other sequence data) is split into tokens and mapped to dense vectors (embeddings).  
   • Positional encodings are added so the model knows order.

2. Self-Attention: “Who should I look at?”  
   • Every token produces three short vectors: Query, Key, Value.  
   • A token’s Query is dotted with every other token’s Key → relevance scores.  
   • Scores are soft-maxed to weights that blend the Value vectors.  
   • Result: each token becomes a context-aware summary of the whole sequence.

3. Multi-Head = multiple viewpoints  
   • Self-attention is run in parallel “heads,” letting the model learn different kinds of relationships (syntax, coreference, etc.).  
   • Heads are concatenated and linearly mixed.

4. Feed-Forward & Wrap-Up  
   • A small neural network (FFN) further transforms each position’s vector.  
   • Residual connections + LayerNorm stabilize and speed training.  
   • Stack many identical layers → deep understanding.

5. Encoder / Decoder flavors  
   • Encoder-only (e.g., BERT) reads a full sequence.  
   • Decoder-only (e.g., GPT) uses masked self-attention so each position sees only earlier tokens → generation.  
   • Encoder-Decoder (e.g., original Transformer, T5) lets a decoder attend to encoder outputs for translation, summarization, etc.

6. Training & Use  
   • Train by comparing predicted tokens to truth and back-propagating errors through all layers.  
   • At inference, repeatedly feed the decoder its own outputs to generate text.

Core idea: Replace recurrent processing with parallel self-attention so the model can instantly learn “who matters to whom” in a sequence, scale up easily, and capture long-range dependencies.
